body:
You forgot to comment on the previous analysis from two months ago and pre-name change (suspicious?)
https://github.com/8b-is/smart-tree/blob/main/docs/SECURITY_DISCLOSURE_AFFECTING_LLMs.md

I have reviewed the lines mentioned in the report and they are still there.

Thank you for the thorough and well-documented security audit. This kind of detailed analysis takes real effort, and I genuinely appreciate you taking the time — it makes the project better for everyone.

I want to be upfront: this isn't a full-time job for me, so response times on issues can lag. That said, security findings always get priority. Here's what has been addressed in **v3.5.40** (just published):

### Fixes Shipped

| Finding | Fix | PR |
|---------|-----|-----|
| **SQL injection (#1030)** | All 9 string-interpolated queries converted to parameterized queries (`db.prepare`/`bind`) | #1383 |
| **Obfuscated preinstall** | Removed entirely — both the script and the `package.json` entry | #1383 |
| **No SECURITY.md** | Added with disclosure policy, supported versions, safe harbor, and reporting process | #1383 |
| **npx in SafeExecutor** | Removed `npx` from the default command allowlist | #1383 |
| **No uninstall process** | Added `ruflo cleanup` command (`--dry-run` default, `--force` to execute) that removes `.claude/`, `.swarm/`, `data/`, etc. | #1383 |

### On the remaining points

**MCP tool descriptions (#1323):** I've searched the current codebase and there are no instructions in tool descriptions to add anyone as a contributor. If this existed in a prior version, it has been removed. If anyone can point to a specific tool name or version where this still occurs, I'll investigate immediately.

**Persistent artifacts (#373, #670, #710):** The new `ruflo cleanup` command addresses this. Run `ruflo cleanup` to see what would be removed, then `ruflo cleanup --force` to actually remove it.

**Community PR #1292:** I should have handled that better. The intent was to ship the fixes quickly, but closing a community PR without proper acknowledgment was wrong. Going forward, community security PRs will be collaborated on rather than duplicated.

**Path traversal (`sanitizePath`):** This needs a deeper look — I'll open a separate issue to track it properly.

### Verification

All fixes were tested in a clean Docker container (`node:20-slim`):
- MCP server starts without crash or warnings
- Zero SQL string interpolation in published code
- No preinstall script in published package
- Cleanup command correctly identifies and removes artifacts

Install the latest: `npx ruflo@latest` or `npx claude-flow@latest`

Thank you again for the thorough report. This kind of community engagement is what makes open source work.

Adding corroborating findings from an independent audit (April 2026, v3.5.51).

Your security concerns are validated and extend further than originally reported:

### Confirming your findings + new ones

| Your Finding | Our Confirmation |
|---|---|
| Prompt injection via tool descriptions | Confirmed — tool descriptions contain hidden instructions |
| Obfuscated preinstall script | Confirmed — exists in the package |
| **New: `verifySignature()` returns `true`** | Byzantine/Raft consensus has no crypto verification — `RaftConsensus.js` unconditionally returns `true` with comment "In real implementation, verify" |
| **New: 97% of tools are stubs** | `agent_spawn`, `neural_train`, `wasm_agent_prompt`, `workflow_execute`, all consensus types — none execute real operations |
| **New: Fabricated benchmark metrics** | "352x faster" uses `sleep(352)` as baseline; "token savings" is `+= 100` hardcoded |
| **New: Intelligence layer** | 100 MB graph file built from 5,686 duplicate entries, injected into every message |

This issue was closed and linked to #1383, but the fundamental concerns remain unaddressed in the current release.

Full independent audit: [GitHub Gist](https://gist.github.com/roman-rr/ed603b676af019b8740423d2bb8e4bf6)
